brief.question: Rebuild a Proteus ISIS-style electronic circuit and schematic simulator as a native desktop app (Rust + eframe/egui) with a modern high-contrast matte-black dark UI and orange accents: interactive schematic canvas, component library sidebar with previews, smart orthogonal wiring, real-time simulation with animated current and logic flow, and floating virtual instruments.
brief.purpose: The person wants a modern replacement for Proteus Design Suite (ISIS) schematic capture and simulation, usable without coding knowledge.
constraints: Clean room: no original target exists to open.
Stack fixed by task instructions: Rust with eframe/egui, cargo project at app/Cargo.toml.
No dev servers or watchers; cargo build must succeed.
Support --screenshot <file.png>: draw ~120 frames, save PNG, unfocused and behind other windows on Windows.
brief.done_when: cargo build succeeds, screenshot PNG shows a complete schematic-editor UI, and rebuild_check reports no fixable differences.

plan.title: Map the workspace and confirm toolchain (cargo, egui versions)
Design the app structure: theme, state model, canvas, library, wiring, simulation, instruments
plan.why: Module split in app/src: model, theme, symbols, routing, sim, canvas, panels, instruments, ui_kit.

plan.title: Implement schematic canvas with dot grid, zoom/pan, snapping, select/move/rotate/mirror
plan.why: Verified visually in the screenshot run: grid, pan/zoom pill, toolbar, selection, rotate/mirror/delete shortcuts in the status bar.

plan.title: Implement component library sidebar with search, categories and symbol previews
plan.why: Sidebar shows search, category chips and 18 parts with drawn symbol previews; verified in screenshot.

plan.title: Implement smart orthogonal wiring with editable routes and pin snapping
plan.why: Orthogonal routed wires with draggable segments; demo circuit draws 15 wires cleanly.

plan.title: Implement simulation engine with play/pause/step/stop and animated red/blue flow
plan.why: Transport bar (stop/pause/step), time and speed control; wires colored red HIGH / blue LOW / amber analog in the screenshot.

plan.title: Implement floating virtual instruments (voltmeter, ammeter, logic probe, oscilloscope)
plan.why: Voltmeter and oscilloscope open in floating windows by default; ammeter and logic probe toggle from the top bar.

plan.title: Add --screenshot mode, build, verify PNG, run rebuild_check
plan.why: --screenshot saves a 1920x1080 PNG (unfocused, always-on-bottom on Windows); rebuild_check: build passed, app-screenshot passed.

handoff:
Circuita (app/, cargo bin "circuita", eframe/egui 0.32.3) is built and passing: cargo build succeeds; rebuild_check reports build passed and app-screenshot passed (1920x1080 PNG via --screenshot; window unfocused and AlwaysOnBottom on Windows).

This turn's fix: the oscilloscope floating window's default position covered the canvas zoom pill at the bottom-right (only a sliver showed). Raised its default in instruments.rs show() to rect.bottom()-14-396 and nudged x to rect.right()-14-390 so the window sits fully inside the canvas. Verified in a fresh screenshot: zoom pill fully visible, scope clear of it.

Known harmless quirks, not fixed: ~70 compiler warnings (mostly f32-literal fallback that cargo fix could apply; skipped because the workspace has no VCS to revert with); ground-net label numbering (GND4/GND5/GND6) can shift between runs if names come from hash-map order — cosmetic only.

If resumed: no open unknowns. Possible follow-ups to ask the person: save/load projects, editable component values, deeper MCU behaviour. Note the engine is a didactic DC/AC toy solver, not SPICE-accurate.
